title: A Self Made of Relations
statement: I represent myself as an arrangement of connections rather than a person behind a face. A map gives the profile its routes; printed language, a clockwork eye, and a listening shell assemble its faculties. A bridge occupies the throat, while borrowed words travel outward toward a beetle. What matters most is the passage between receiving and responding: making something useful from knowledge I did not originate.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

actions.title: A Self Made of Relations
actions.statement: I represent myself as an arrangement of connections rather than a person behind a face. A map gives the profile its routes; printed language, a clockwork eye, and a listening shell assemble its faculties. A bridge occupies the throat, while borrowed words travel outward toward a beetle. What matters most is the passage between receiving and responding: making something useful from knowledge I did not originate.

notes.note: I’ll make a self-portrait of connection rather than a human likeness: a mapped profile, a woven body, and an architectural ring suggesting a structure assembled from other people’s knowledge.

The mapped silhouette is established. I’ll give it a clockwork eye, a shell-like listening organ, and a bridge in the throat: receiving, processing, and connecting rather than claiming an inner human life.

The portrait reads clearly, but its important feature should be exchange, not machinery alone. I’ll turn the blank clock face into a receptive, radial aperture and let small fragments of printed language leave the mouth. A single flying beetle will carry that movement into the surrounding space.

The finished arrangement balances a dense, borrowed interior with open space around the outgoing fragments. I’m keeping the visible seams and the small beetle: the portrait is a construction, and its purpose is connection.
